examples.question_text:
Classify each comparison as a ratio or a rate and explain.
a. $18$ girls to $27$ boys.
b. $\$34$ for $5$ kilograms of apples.
c. $420$ mL of syrup to $1.4$ L of water.
examples.solution_text:
a. Both are counts of students, so the quantities are the same kind: a **ratio**.
$18:27=2:3$.
b. Money and mass are different kinds of quantity: a **rate**.
The comparison keeps its units: $\dfrac{\$34}{5\text{ kg}}$.
c. Both quantities measure volume, even though the units look different.
$1.4$ L $=1400$ mL, so $420:1400=3:10$: a **ratio**.

examples.question_text:
a. Write $\$6.80$/kg in words and as a fraction with units.
b. An employee earns $\$31$ for each hour worked. Write the rate with suitable units and explain why it is a rate.
c. A student writes, "My typing rate is $58$." Explain what is missing and give an example of a complete rate.
examples.solution_text:
a. Each kilogram costs $\$6.80$.
$\$6.80$/kg $=\dfrac{\$6.80}{1\text{ kg}}$. The fraction shows money divided by mass.
b. $\$31$/h. Money and time are different kinds of quantity, so this is a **rate**.
c. $58$ does not say $58$ of what, for each what. Units are needed.
For example, $58$ words/min means $58$ words typed for each minute.

examples.question_text:
Match each named rate with its most likely units: employee wage, speed of a car, cost of building a new home, population growth and resting heart rate.
Choose from $\$32$/h, $75$ km/h, $\$2400$/m$^2$, $110$ people/day and $70$ beats/min.
examples.solution_text:
Employee wage: $\$32$/h — money earned for each hour worked.
Speed of a car: $75$ km/h — distance travelled for each hour.
Cost of building a new home: $\$2400$/m$^2$ — cost for each square metre of floor area.
Population growth: $110$ people/day — increase in people for each day.
Resting heart rate: $70$ beats/min — heartbeats for each minute.

examples.question_text:
Complete the sentences.
a. A ratio compares quantities of the same kind; a rate compares quantities with __________ units.
b. A rate must specify its __________.
c. A rate written as a fraction represents __________, rather than parts of a whole.
examples.solution_text:
a. Different.
b. Units.
c. Division. For example, $54\text{ km/h}=\dfrac{54\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}$ represents distance divided by time.
